usedCounterFrames: ch01 counter must contrast Treating the three conversations as a tidy checklist or as the solution itself. with Separate a recent hard exchange into its facts, feelings, and identity layers before choosing any response.
ch02 counter must contrast Being nicer while still trying to deliver a verdict. with Hold your story as one coherent version and ask what the other person sees that your position cannot see.
ch03 counter must contrast Assuming good intentions are enough or treating hurt feelings as proof of malice. with Acknowledge the impact as real before explaining what you meant.

ch04 counter must contrast False parity, self-blame, or using contribution language to excuse the person with more power. with Map the repeating contribution system and identify one move of yours that keeps it alive.
ch05 counter must contrast Dumping emotion or suppressing it in the name of professionalism. with Translate a vague or disguised feeling into a direct report you can own.

ch06 counter must contrast Using AND/BOTH as self-soothing language that prevents feedback from leaving a mark. with Ground the threatened identity belief before the conversation by making it complex enough to hold bad news.
ch07 counter must contrast Raising every grievance because honesty sounds virtuous. with Choose a conversation only when its honest purpose is something that conversation can actually produce.
ch08 counter must contrast Softening an accusation while leaving your story as the baseline. with Start from a neutral description of the gap between views and invite comparison rather than defense.
ch09 counter must contrast Equating listening with silence, eye contact, or scripted paraphrase. with Set down the internal voice long enough for the other person's meaning to arrive.
ch10 counter must contrast Generic assertiveness or softer accusations labeled as I-statements. with Report your experience as discussable material without turning your interpretation into a verdict.

ch11 counter must contrast Jumping to fix the issue before understanding and expression have happened. with Lead the process of solving together without taking ownership of the solution away from the other person.
ch12 counter must contrast Recapping a checklist or performing the framework mechanically. with Compose the right move for the live situation while staying genuinely open to what may change.
usedTryThisNowFrames: Take one avoided conversation and write three labels: what happened, feelings, identity. Put one concrete stake under each label before planning any words.
Rewrite the sentence you most want to deliver as one question whose answer could genuinely alter your view.
Draft the first reply to someone you hurt with impact first and intent second. Delete any sentence that tries to make intent settle impact.
Draw the repeating loop in one stuck conflict and put a small star beside the move you personally keep making.
Replace one vague feeling word with three more exact feelings, then turn one into a direct self-report without the phrase 'like you.'
Name the identity belief most threatened by one conversation and write its AND/BOTH version before you rehearse the talk.
Write the purpose of one possible conversation, then cross out any part aimed at winning, punishment, or changing who they are.
Draft a third-story opener that the other person could recognize as plausible even while disagreeing with your view.
In the next tense exchange, silently label your internal voice as counterargument, judgment, or identity before asking one real question.
Turn one accusation into three owned parts: observable event, internal response, and the story you started telling yourself.
Before offering a fix, list three possible options and one standard both sides would accept before seeing the options.
Pick the avoided conversation and sketch the sequence: raise or let go, prepare, open, listen, speak, solve, close.
